main.title: Fortnite
main.subtitle: From cooperative defence to a platform of worlds
main.summary: Fortnite began in 2017 with cooperative defence and a battle royale mode, then expanded into a platform for player-built worlds and other genres.

cards.heading: One game in many forms
cards.text: Fortnite is an online game developed and published by Epic Games. Save the World combines shooting, resource gathering and fortification building against waves of creatures. Battle Royale sends up to one hundred players into a last-survivor contest. Later additions included Creative?s player-built arenas, Lego Fortnite?s building and survival, the rhythm game Fortnite Festival and Rocket Racing.

cards.heading: From Save the World to Battle Royale
cards.text: Save the World and Battle Royale were released in 2017 as early access titles, while Creative was released on December 6, 2018. While Save the World and Creative versions have been successful for Epic Games, Fortnite Battle Royale in particular became an overwhelming success and a cultural phenomenon, drawing more than 125 million players in less than a year and earning hundreds of millions of dollars per month. Fortnite as a whole generated $9 billion in gross revenue up until December 2019, making it one of the highest-grossing media franchises of all time. Since its release, Fortnite has been listed among the greatest video games of all time.

cards.heading: Platforms and playing together
cards.text: Fortnite began on computers, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One before expanding across consoles and mobile devices. Cross-platform play lets friends on supported systems join the same matches. New modes broadened the activities available within the game.

cards.heading: Seasons and chapters
cards.text: Battle Royale changes through seasons grouped into Chapters. These updates bring new locations, events and adjustments to the island, giving returning players different terrain and challenges.

main.title: Dragon Quest XI
main.subtitle: A persecuted hero in the world of Erdrea
main.summary: Dragon Quest XI follows the Luminary, a persecuted young hero, through the world of Erdrea. Square Enix first released it in Japan for PlayStation 4 and Nintendo 3DS in July 2017.

cards.heading: The Luminary’s journey
cards.text: Dragon Quest XI: Echoes of an Elusive Age is a role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix. It launched in Japan for PlayStation 4 and Nintendo 3DS in July 2017, reaching Western PS4 and Windows players in September 2018. The hero travels through Erdrea to prevent an approaching disaster while facing persecution over his identity as the prophesied Luminary. The later XI S edition expanded the story and added an orchestral score option.

cards.heading: A tradition opens to the West
cards.text: One of the first games announced for the Switch, the game was originally conceived to be fully open world; however, the idea was scrapped when it conflicted with the story the developers wanted to tell. To increase the awareness of the Dragon Quest franchise in the West, support for Windows and features such as voiced English dialogue and 4K resolution were included. Elements added later included an expanded plot and an option to listen to an orchestral version of the score.

cards.heading: Reception and legacy
cards.text: Upon release, the game received critical acclaim for its story, characters, narrative, and localization, though its design was criticized for being overly traditional. The game has shipped over 9 million copies as of September 2025. The Luminary has also been featured in crossover media such as Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.

main.title: The Great Ace Attorney 2: Resolve
main.subtitle: The defence returns to an unfinished case
main.summary: The Great Ace Attorney 2: Resolve is Capcom's Nintendo 3DS courtroom adventure continuing Ryunosuke Naruhodo's story in Japan and Britain. Following the first game's unresolved questions, it brings the returning defence team into cases whose connections extend beyond an individual hearing. Susato Mikotoba and Herlock Sholmes remain central companions as the investigation develops. The sequel gives the historical setting a longer narrative structure, allowing details introduced in earlier encounters to acquire new significance when another witness, piece of evidence or account changes what they appeared to mean.

cards.heading: The defence returns to an unfinished case
cards.text: The Great Ace Attorney 2: Resolve is Capcom's Nintendo 3DS courtroom adventure continuing Ryunosuke Naruhodo's story in Japan and Britain. Following the first game's unresolved questions, it brings the returning defence team into cases whose connections extend beyond an individual hearing. Susato Mikotoba and Herlock Sholmes remain central companions as the investigation develops. The sequel gives the historical setting a longer narrative structure, allowing details introduced in earlier encounters to acquire new significance when another witness, piece of evidence or account changes what they appeared to mean.

cards.heading: Listen to the people sharing the stand
cards.text: Cross-examinations can place several witnesses together, allowing one person's testimony to provoke a response from another. The player watches those reactions and follows them into further questions, comparing accounts rather than treating each speaker as an isolated source. Evidence still provides the means to challenge a contradiction. The group arrangement adds another reason to pay attention between formal statements: hesitation or surprise may indicate that someone knows more than the current testimony admits. Understanding the relationship between witnesses becomes part of understanding the event they describe.

cards.heading: A deduction can open the next question
cards.text: Dance of Deduction sequences again require Ryunosuke to correct Sholmes's reasoning by examining the details around him. British hearings also retain Summation Examination, where conflicting reasons offered by jurors can be set against one another. These systems provide several routes into the same task of testing an explanation. Resolve uses the returning methods across a story designed to conclude the pair of adventures. The familiar gestures gain weight because a newly established fact can affect an older mystery, giving careful observation consequences beyond the immediate courtroom exchange.

main.title: Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice
main.subtitle: Senua’s journey
main.summary: Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice is a 2017 action-adventure game developed and published by Ninja Theory.

cards.heading: Senua’s journey
cards.text: Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice is a 2017 action-adventure game developed and published by Ninja Theory. It is the first installment in the Hellblade series. It was released for PlayStation 4 and Windows in August 2017, Xbox One in April 2018, Nintendo Switch in April 2019, Xbox Series X/S in August 2021, and PlayStation 5 in August 2025. Hellblade features support for virtual reality, which was added in a 2018 update.

cards.heading: Toward Helheim
cards.text: Set in a dark fantasy world inspired by Norse mythology and Celtic culture, the game follows Senua, a Pict warrior who must make her way to Helheim by defeating otherworldly entities and facing their challenges, in order to rescue the soul of her dead lover from the goddess Hela.

cards.heading: A small team with AAA ambition
cards.text: Self-described as an "independent AAA game", Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice was created by a team of approximately twenty developers led by writer and director Tameem Antoniades. The game blends different gameplay mechanics and concepts like puzzle solving, psychological horror and melee combat. Voice acting is an integral part of the game, while its cutscenes combine motion capture by Melina Juergens, and live action performances by other actors. The game's narrative serves as a metaphor for the character's struggle with psychosis, as Senua, who suffers from the condition but believes it to be a curse, is haunted by an entity known as the "Darkness", voices in her head known as "Furies", and memories from her past. To properly represent psychosis, developers worked closely with neuroscientists, mental health specialists, and people living with the condition.

cards.heading: The power of a performance
cards.text: Reviewers praised the story, presentation and Melina Juergens? performance as Senua, alongside the care taken in representing psychosis. Reactions to the combat and other gameplay elements were more mixed. The game sold more than a million copies by June 2018, and Senua?s Saga: Hellblade II followed in May 2024.

main.title: Matterfall
main.subtitle: A battle suit moves through a world of unstable matter
main.summary: Matterfall is Housemarque's PlayStation 4 side-scrolling shooter, first released in North America on 15 August 2017. Avalon Darrow fights through a futuristic world infected by alien Smart Matter, using an armoured suit to jump, dodge and fire at the surrounding threats. The player also creates platforms and protective structures, making the environment part of the available response. A dangerous space can therefore be altered as well as crossed. The game connects precise shooting to platform movement, asking the player to see where safety might be constructed while the next attack is already approaching.

The game connects precise shooting to platform movement, asking the player to see where safety might be constructed while the next attack is already approaching.

cards.heading: Make the route while clearing the threat
cards.text: Platform creation gives the player a way to turn the surrounding material into something useful, opening a position or approach that would otherwise be unavailable. Shields offer another intervention when ordinary movement does not provide enough protection. The player has to connect those capabilities with firing and dodging, recognising when to keep attacking and when the shape of the encounter should be changed first. The side-on presentation makes those relationships visible together. A platform is not merely a place supplied by the designer, but can become part of the player's immediate solution to a dangerous arrangement.

cards.heading: Housemarque combines two arcade habits
cards.text: Tommi Hartikainen directed the project, with Jari Hokkanen designing. Announced at Paris Games Week in 2015, it reached PlayStation 4 in August 2017, with a soundtrack and console theme offered among its preorder extras. Critical responses were mixed, but the design continued Housemarque's interest in immediate action whose depth comes from combining a small number of abilities under pressure. Matterfall gives that approach a side-scrolling form, joining the demands of keeping a firing line clear to the physical problem of reaching a useful position while enemies and projectiles occupy the same space.

main.title: Sonic Mania
main.subtitle: A return to the roots
main.summary: Sonic Mania is a 2017 platform game developed by Christian Whitehead, PagodaWest Games and Headcannon and published by Sega.

cards.heading: Old zones and new routes for Sonic
cards.text: Sonic Mania is a 2017 platform game developed by Christian Whitehead, PagodaWest Games and Headcannon and published by Sega. Produced in commemoration of the Sonic the Hedgehog series' 25th anniversary, Sonic Mania pays homage to the original Sega Genesis Sonic games, featuring speedy side-scrolling gameplay. It takes place over 13 levels, including several redesigned from past games. The story follows Sonic, Tails and Knuckles as they venture to defeat Doctor Eggman and his robotic henchmen, the Hard-Boiled Heavies.

cards.heading: A team formed in the fan community
cards.text: The development team was composed of members known for their work in the Sonic fangame and ROM hacking community. Development began after lead developer, director and programmer Christian "Taxman" Whitehead, who was previously contracted by Sega to develop enhanced mobile ports of Genesis Sonic games, presented a playable prototype to Sonic Team producer Takashi Iizuka. Art, level design, audio, and additional programming were provided by independent studios PagodaWest Games and Headcannon. The team used Whitehead's Retro Engine and aimed for a graphical quality between Genesis and Sega Saturn games.

cards.heading: A return to form and an expanded edition
cards.text: Sonic Mania was released in August 2017 for the Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, Xbox One and Windows. It became the highest-rated Sonic game in fifteen years; many reviewers saw it as a return to form following a number of poorly received games released after the 1990s. Its presentation, level design, music, and faithfulness to the early Sonic games were praised, but its lack of originality was criticized. Several critics named it one of the best Sonic games and one of the best games of 2017. Within a year, it had sold over one million copies. Sonic Mania Plus, an enhanced version with additional content, was released in July 2018.

main.title: Uncharted: The Lost Legacy
main.subtitle: An adventure for Chloe and Nadine
main.summary: Uncharted: The Lost Legacy is a 2017 action-adventure game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment, serving as a standalone expansion to the 2016 game Uncharted 4: A Thief's End.

cards.heading: Chloe and Nadine in the Western Ghats
cards.text: Uncharted: The Lost Legacy is a 2017 action-adventure game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment, serving as a standalone expansion to the 2016 game Uncharted 4: A Thief's End. Players control Chloe Frazer, who seeks the Tusk of Ganesh in the Western Ghats mountain ranges of India, with the help of ex-mercenary Nadine Ross, and prevent a ruthless warlord and his army of insurgents from igniting a civil war in the country. It is the first Uncharted game not to feature series protagonist Nathan Drake. Like other Uncharted games, The Lost Legacy is played from a third-person perspective; players use firearms and can use melee combat and stealth to defend against enemies. Players solve puzzles, incorporating several platformer elements to advance the narrative, and navigate the game world on foot or by vehicle.

cards.heading: Building a different Uncharted partnership
cards.text: Development of The Lost Legacy began soon after the release of A Thief's End in May 2016. It builds upon gameplay elements established in previous Uncharted titles with its more open-ended gameplay. Chloe, a supporting character who appeared in previous Uncharted games as a friend, love interest, and associate to Nathan Drake, is the focus of the game, with the story, design, and gameplay elements reflecting her character. Claudia Black, Laura Bailey and Troy Baker reprised their roles as Chloe, Nadine and Samuel Drake respectively, through voice and motion capture, and assisted writer Josh Scherr and creative director Shaun Escayg with the development of the characters and story.

main.title: Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle
main.subtitle: A comic collision becomes a tactics game
main.summary: Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle is Ubisoft Milan and Ubisoft Paris's tactical adventure, released for Switch on 29 August 2017.

cards.heading: A comic collision becomes a tactics game
cards.text: Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle is Ubisoft Milan and Ubisoft Paris's tactical adventure, released for Switch on 29 August 2017. Mario and his friends join Rabbid counterparts after a mishap transforms the Mushroom Kingdom. The journey alternates exploration and puzzles with turn-based battles, giving familiar characters another way to cooperate. Bright environments and exaggerated animation make the crossover immediately comic, while each arena asks a concrete tactical question: where to move a small team so that its attacks and protection work together.

cards.heading: Movement is part of the attack
cards.text: The player selects a squad whose characters offer different weapons and abilities. Cover changes the risk of a position, while movement can contribute directly to an attack or help a teammate reach another part of the arena. Planning a turn therefore involves more than choosing a target. The useful route may connect several actions before the final shot, making cooperation visible in the characters' movement. The battlefield gives a clear space in which to test that plan and see how the opponents respond on their turn.

cards.heading: Ubisoft builds another Mushroom Kingdom
cards.text: Director Davide Soliani and producer Xavier Manzanares began shaping the project in 2014, pursuing a strategy game that could draw on the differences between its two worlds. Grant Kirkhope composed the music. Four main environments connect the battles through exploration, with Beep-0 gaining new puzzle-solving abilities as the adventure advances. A Donkey Kong expansion followed in 2018. The original game's identity comes from making those unlikely partners useful to one another, joining a carefully arranged tactical encounter to the visual playfulness of the Mushroom Kingdom.

main.title: Everybody's Golf
main.subtitle: A golf course becomes a place to spend time
main.summary: Everybody's Golf is Clap Hanz and Japan Studio's PlayStation 4 sports game, first released in North America on 29 August 2017. The series' accessible shot-making returns inside courses that can be explored more freely, with a created golfer taking part in the wider setting. Players can walk around and drive golf carts instead of treating each hole only as the next isolated screen. That freedom gives the surroundings another role. A course is still a sequence of sporting problems, but it also becomes a place whose shape and routes can be encountered between shots.

cards.text: Everybody's Golf is Clap Hanz and Japan Studio's PlayStation 4 sports game, first released in North America on 29 August 2017. The series' accessible shot-making returns inside courses that can be explored more freely, with a created golfer taking part in the wider setting. Players can walk around and drive golf carts instead of treating each hole only as the next isolated screen. That freedom gives the surroundings another role. A course is still a sequence of sporting problems, but it also becomes a place whose shape and routes can be encountered between shots.

cards.heading: Read the hole before committing to the swing
cards.text: The approachable presentation leaves room for attention to distance, terrain and the desired landing position. A successful shot depends on choosing an appropriate approach and carrying it out consistently, with later attempts making a familiar hole easier to judge. The player develops a personal golfer while encountering different conditions and challenges. Exploration gives another way to understand the layout, connecting the visible landscape to the decisions made during play. The game keeps the distinction between an easy-to-understand action and the longer process of learning where that action should send the ball.

cards.heading: A long-running series opens out
cards.text: The PlayStation 4 release followed years of Everybody's Golf games across Sony consoles and handhelds. Its character creation and open elements were presented as a new direction when the project was announced in 2014. Clap Hanz developed it with Japan Studio, maintaining the series' bright visual character and accessible entry point. Online play originally extended the social setting beyond the local course. Its particular contribution is the way it loosens the spaces between shots, allowing a traditionally structured sports game to include the less directed pleasure of simply being around the course with other people.

main.title: Knack II
main.subtitle: A changing body gives the adventure another scale
main.summary: Knack II is Japan Studio's PlayStation 4 action-platform game, first released in North America on 5 September 2017. Knack and his companions investigate a threat connected to the High-Goblins and ancient weapons, with the hero's ability to change size shaping the journey. Combat, platforming and environmental puzzles sit beside a more developed set of attacks and upgrades. The sequel also makes cooperative play a central feature, allowing another person to join the story. A recognisable character becomes the basis for an adventure intended to be shared by players with different levels of experience.

cards.text: Knack II is Japan Studio's PlayStation 4 action-platform game, first released in North America on 5 September 2017. Knack and his companions investigate a threat connected to the High-Goblins and ancient weapons, with the hero's ability to change size shaping the journey. Combat, platforming and environmental puzzles sit beside a more developed set of attacks and upgrades. The sequel also makes cooperative play a central feature, allowing another person to join the story. A recognisable character becomes the basis for an adventure intended to be shared by players with different levels of experience.

cards.heading: Choose the size and ability the obstacle requires
cards.text: Knack punches, kicks and deflects projectiles, while collected energy develops a skill tree and opens further possibilities. Changing size allows a space to be read differently, turning the body itself into one of the tools used to continue. Special forms such as Iron, Ice and Stealth alter both appearance and function. Treasure chests supply parts for additional upgrades, giving exploration another practical reward. The player learns when force is useful and when the next problem asks for a smaller shape or a particular ability, connecting development to the environment rather than only increasing damage.

cards.heading: Make it easier for another person to take part
cards.text: A second local player can join or leave during the campaign, reducing the interruption involved in sharing the adventure. Takamitsu Iijima directed, Marianne Krawczyk and Mark Cerny wrote, and Anthony Willis composed the music. Reviews were mixed but generally regarded the sequel as an improvement on the original. Its cooperative structure gives the series a clearer social purpose. One player can help another through the same journey without requiring two separate campaigns or a strict commitment from the beginning, making the changing character's adventure something the people beside the television can enter together.
